Skeleton's TreeEditor was implemented in #36409, but the gizmo for editing was not (ref: [584](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/584) and [#1767](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1767)). So, the gizmo in `SkeletonEditor`, which was developed in the 3.2.x branch, is now complete tentatively. This is a draft PR for porting to 4.0.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjJiEo8uqPw

Dev branch for 3.2.x is [here](https://github.com/TokageItLab/godot/tree/pose-edit-mode).

## Features

![pr1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/106864740-a119f200-670d-11eb-949e-035335f65b48.png)

When you select skeleton and bone edit tool, marker circles will appear on the joints. If you select a marker, a transform gizmo will appear, ~which looks the same as `SpatialTransformGizmo` but behaves a bit differently. Basically, in character animation, there is no editing other than rotate. So to make the editing process smoother, you can make selections in all `Move/Rotate/Scale` modes. Instead, there is no free transform mode, which I may implement somewhere else.~ the behavior was unified by SubGizmo implementation.

![pr2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/106864763-a6773c80-670d-11eb-8030-edd671b8c634.gif)

There is a `PoseMode` and a `RestMode`; during `RestMode`, `Pose` and `CustomPose` are temporarily disabled, and `RestMode` will be canceled when you exit the `SkeletonEditor`. However, there is no `CustomPoseMode`, because there is no way to disable only the `Pose` while the `CustomPose` is enabled.

![pr3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/106864775-a9722d00-670d-11eb-8b28-a71f596c5db6.png)

Add the following options to `SkeletonButton`'s popups in toolber

- Init pose
- Insert key of all bone poses
- Insert key of bone poses already exist track
- Apply current pose to rest

All of these are basically applied to all bones. *Init pose* initializes the Pose, but not the `CustomPose`. *Insert key* is activated when the animation player has a track, similar to `Spatial`'s `KeyButton`. Be careful with *Apply current pose to rest*. It initializes the current `Pose` and `CustomPose`, and changes `Rest`.

## Changes/Bugfixes

### SkeletonEditor
- Added `int selected_bone`
- Removed the *Pose Enabled* checkbox in `SkeletonBoneEditor` to prevent conflicts in `RestMode`

### SpatialEditorGizmo
- Skeleton's gizmo is now at the front of the screen when skeleton is selected
- Show the local axis of the bones when selecting a skeleton
- Highlight the currently selected bone
- Added *selected bone color* and *bone axis length* to `EditorSettings`

### SpatialEditorPlugin
- ~Added `Vector<Transform> external`~
- ~Added `ToolExternal` to `ToolMode`~
- ~`forward_spatial_gui_input()` passes the id of the Viewport~
- ~Some private functions changed to public~

These were superseded SubGizmo implementation.

### AnimationTrackEditor
- Added `has_transform_track()`

## Done

- [x] Porting for 4.0
- [x] Fix depth drawing order in gizmo (with the shader by @lyuma )
- [x] Consider the size and shape of the joint marker
- [x] Adopt SubGizmos
- [x] Behavior for negative scales is not ensured
- [x] Set readonly to bone pose in rest mode after marge #51722
- [x] Octahedron as bone gizmo in `SpatialEditorGizmo` weight assignment and updated timing are strange (superseded selectable gizmo shape with Wire shape)

## Other Issues (Todo in the future)
- ~~Need to fix some function (inserting multiple tracks has been broken) #51459~~ Fixed
- `SkeletonEditor` does not support multiple selection
- Need independent bone handling (with changing skin pose) in edit rest option for adjust initial rest
- ~~#52627~~ Fixed

Is it a good idea to draw the skeleton not using skinning? I have the feeling this may have quite serious performance implications

I agree we should change the gizmo to avoid the skew, I suppose any shape that works makes sense.
@reduz When using skinning, the only shape that doesn't cause Skew is the Wire shape, anyway, but how do you feel about adopting that?

Also, there is an error that vulkan's free() fails due to the gizmo skinning. As I mentioned above, there is no performance concern except for tools, so I think one way is to use a method that does not use skinning.

There are 4 possible ways to prevent Skew. 

1. As it is now, we omit Skinning and redraw gizmo when pose_update.

2. Use Skinning and adopt the Wire shape.

3. Use Skinning to define an arbitrary shape as one of the `RenderingServer::PrimitiveType` and draw it on the `RenderingServer`.

4. Implement Compute Shaders and draw arbitrary shapes with Shaders.

@reduz 3 and 4 are out of the scope of this PR. If you plan to adopt these, it makes sense to choice 2 as a preparation of these. However, in terms of ease of viewing and using, I would recommend 1, with the following in mind:

> Also, there is an error that vulkan's free() fails due to the gizmo skinning. As I mentioned above, there is no performance concern except for tools, so I think one way is to use a method that does not use skinning.

I would like to note that the heavy work in `Skeleton3DGizmoPlugin::redraw` is the call to `get_bone_global_pose` since this talks to the RenderingServer and the `.inverse()` on each basis for drawing the coordinate axes.

If there is performance concern, I'd suggest just adding a `LocalVector<Transform3D>` at the top for calculating the bone global poses directly to avoid the expensive `get_global_bone_pose`, and maybe only do the inverse() once per bone, rather than once per axis.

If this is done, it's basically a small and constant amount of vector math per bone, the heaviest of which is 6 cross products: 2 per axis. (As well as the cost of calculating global bone pose matrices, which is unavoidable.)

In terms of the number of vertices, it looks something like 38 per vertex. Assuming a rig with 300 bones, that's 10000 vertices produced per frame, which should be no problem on the CPU. It's also very much proportional to the cost of calculating the 300 bone matrices on the CPU that would need to be copied to the GPU for a skinning pass.

Therefore, the way things are, I do not think a skinning pass is a worthwhile option to pursue. It will become necessary when we have scenes with hundreds of skeletons in a single editor scene. I'd like to wait for the usecase to be presented so we have a real world benchmark to base performance improvements on.

As Lyuma said, it makes sense to do it in a way that avoids access to `get_bone_global_pose()`.

However, there have been PRs posted in the past with suggestions for improving `get_bone_global_pose()`, but which is currently in limbo.

- #41322
- #42681

I think it is necessary to salvage them anyway, and I think current skeleton gizmo method will be possible to adapt to them salvaged later, and which is good for other methods that use `get_bone_global_pose()`.

@TokageItLab If I have to be completely honest, and thinking about it, I dont mind the bone skewing very much, I think this pretty much information anyway, and its rare to actually see this happening in practice. If you do, it may also be an indicative of a mistake or error in the model. Godot is not really a 3D modelling app anyway.

@lyuma it does not scale, its common to see complex models use thousands of bones for stuff like cinematics, we need to entirely avoid doing this using CPU.

With the implementation of the Skeleton Manipulator, the selected SkeletonGizmo is now in the foreground, and making it easier to manipulate the bones. It may makes sense for skew to occur with Scaling, but I think it's completely wrong for skew to occur with Translating. Also, although Godot is not a 3D modeling software, it is necessary to understand the bone structure correctly in order to animate it.

The global rest calculation is broken because the processing order has been changed in `Skeleton3D::register_skin()`. So we can solve this problem by implementing a readonly parameter called global_rest in the skeleton, similar to global_pose, or it may be better to revert the processing order array for the global rest and calculate it as needed.

It seems that reduz is thinking of getting rid of the bone rest. He has a point since it may be not good to allow users to easily handle posing with bone rests. However, when it comes to retargeting or adjusting axes, rest needs to be changed.

Therefore, it would be better to omit the implementation of rest mode bone manipulation, and make rest and custom poses read only in the inspector, and instead add a "Rest Option" in the 3D View menu, such as operating "Set global rest", "Unify roll axis to specific axis", "Swap axis" and etc  (everything will do with changing the skin poses).

As a followup to the idea of removing bone_rest as it currently is... and just jotting down some thoughts I had recently: I've been increasingly thinking that rest_pose should become an animation concept of some sort, and added to "rotation", "position" and "scale" type tracks.

Basically, Animations could use the rest matrix (transform/rotation/scale) applied one after the other, so there is no problem with non-uniform matrices but you can still assign "identity" tracks in the animation to reset the object to the rest pose.

Another option is for the animation transform track to be separated into animation position track, rotation track and scale track (note that a Transform track internally already stores data in this form, but it requires all 10 values to be set, even though most animations only change rotation)... that way, the position would remain unchanged and the bone rest does not need to be stored.

Why does this use embeded bone data instead of BoneAttachment3D?
And why can't we convert our meshes as relative children to the BoneAttachment3D's?

I do not understand what you are asking. FYI, as to why all bones should not  be the children of the scene as an actual Node. It is written in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1767 because it is mainly from a performance point of view.

If you want to generate BoneAttachment from multiple bones, I remember it is possible to add it when setting up PhysicalBone, but I don't think there was a way to add only BoneAttachment. You can open a proposal for that.

If you want to convert a gizmo to a MeshInstance, that doesn't make sense. Most 3D applications don't have that capability and Godot is the same. That doesn't have to be included in the core as a general feature. I know that Blender has such a thing as an 3rd party addon for that, so I suggest you look for an addon or make your own.

issue_context.title: Inserting multiple tracks in `AnimationTrackEditor` is broken
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev

### System information

MacOS 11.4

### Issue description

`_query_insert()` in `AnimationTrackEditor` used to be able to insert multiple tracks, but now it doesn't work. From my investigation, it determines if the insertions were done on the same frame and summarizes the operations. It seems that the renderer or GUI process has changed and is no longer working. It is regression, but I think it is not good implementation of "determine if it's the same frame" in the first place, so it needs to be improved.

### Steps to reproduce

Try to insert multiple animations at the same time with iteration in `AnimationTrackEditor` c++. GDScript doesn't have direct access to `AnimationTrackEditor` and calls to its functions, but this has been a problem when implement function of inserting track to the engine side such as #45699.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_

review_comments: Ideally the drawing of handles would also happen in the gizmos `redraw()`, but we can leave this for a later PR, it's not critical.
This is like a wrapper function to avoid errors due to bone update timing. It might be better to rename the function.
For now, I'll leave it in place.

I would make this consistent with `Control::MouseFilter`, something like Pass, Stop and Deselect (after a quick search in godot's code, deselect seems to be used instead of unselect). 

Also, the values themselves need to contain the enum's name, just like all enums in Godot. That would result in:
`AFTER_GUI_INPUT_PASS`,
`AFTER_GUI_INPUT_STOP`,
`AFTER_GUI_INPUT_DESELECT`

which is a bit long, maybe we can rename the enum to be `EventFilter`, and keep it consistent with `Control::MouseFilter`? not sure abut this one.
For now, I renamed it to `AFTER_GUI_INPUT_PASS`, `AFTER_GUI_INPUT_STOP`, `AFTER_GUI_INPUT_DESELECT`.
